name: fema-disaster-information
what_it_holds: Analysis repo combining FEMA Disaster Declarations and Public Assistance data, with committed extracts/notebooks (per repo description: 'FEMA Disaster Declarations and Public Assistance Data Analysis').
why_useful: Reasonably popular, MIT-licensed reference implementation for pulling/analysing OpenFEMA declarations and public-assistance grant data, another route into gap 11 with more community traction than the rearc-data pipeline repo.
themes: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets
why_all: Reasonably popular, MIT-licensed reference implementation for pulling/analysing OpenFEMA declarations and public-assistance grant data, another route into gap 11 with more community traction than the rearc-data pipeline repo.

Secondary/smaller alternative to the rearc-data mirror; worth a quick look if that one's AWS Data Exchange dependency is inconvenient, since Public Assistance $ amounts by disaster give a rough severity/dollar-cost proxy per event.

name: emdatr
what_it_holds: R package (CRAN mirror) 'Global disaster losses from the EM-DAT database' -- functions to load/process EM-DAT (CRED Université catholique de Louvain) global natural-disaster loss records (deaths, affected population, damage estimates) by country/year/disaster-type.
why_useful: Direct EM-DAT tooling named in the theme's own keyword hints; EM-DAT itself is licensed/registration-gated at source (no full open GitHub mirror was found), so this is the closest thing to a reusable open client, though the package itself is old (2015) and would need a fresh EM-DAT export to be useful today.
time_coverage: EM-DAT coverage as of package's last CRAN sync (~2015); underlying EM-DAT goes back to 1900
duplicate_of_holding: none held; EM-DAT itself not otherwise in our holdings
themes: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets
why_all: Direct EM-DAT tooling named in the theme's own keyword hints; EM-DAT itself is licensed/registration-gated at source (no full open GitHub mirror was found), so this is the closest thing to a reusable open client, though the package itself is old (2015) and would need a fresh EM-DAT export to be useful today.

name: wildfire-perimeters
what_it_holds: Showcase app exploring STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) fire-event data hosted by NASA's VEDA (Visualization, Exploration, and Data Analysis) platform -- points to VEDA's own fire-event STAC collections rather than committing data itself.
why_useful: Points to NASA VEDA's STAC fire-event catalog, a modern queryable geospatial index of US fire events that could be pulled directly (via STAC API) for perimeter + date without needing firedpy's local MODIS processing.
time_coverage: per VEDA's own fire-event STAC catalog coverage
size_hint: showcase app; data lives on NASA VEDA (https://openveda.cloud)
themes: Weather, hurricanes, wildfires, disasters: NOAA/NHC tracks, EM-DAT, FEMA declarations, wildfire perimeters (Maui, LA fires), heatwaves; tourism-shock datasets
why_all: Points to NASA VEDA's STAC fire-event catalog, a modern queryable geospatial index of US fire events that could be pulled directly (via STAC API) for perimeter + date without needing firedpy's local MODIS processing.

name: TravelAdvisoryScraper
what_it_holds: A Python scraper (BeautifulSoup4/Requests/Pandas) that pulls Canada's official government travel advisory website and writes a CSV of current advisory levels by destination country. No data is committed to the repo (gitignored output); includes an AWS Lambda branch for scheduled cloud runs.
why_useful: A second-country (Canada) travel-advisory data source, complementary to the US State Dept feed, giving a different vantage point on the same demand-shock signal -- low marginal value alone but a working method that could be scheduled to build a point-in-time series if run going forward (not run per the sanctioned-sources rule).
time_coverage: current snapshot only, no historical data committed
themes: Insurance, safety and travel advisories datasets (State Dept advisories history, travel insurance claims, crime by city) as demand shocks
why_all: A second-country (Canada) travel-advisory data source, complementary to the US State Dept feed, giving a different vantage point on the same demand-shock signal -- low marginal value alone but a working method that could be scheduled to build a point-in-time series if run going forward (not run per the sanctioned-sources rule).

name: global_peace
what_it_holds: Committed Global Peace Index dataset (country-level peace/safety scores) plus Python data-viz scripts. Small repo (2 stars), scope and exact year range not confirmed beyond the description; appears to be a static snapshot of GPI country rankings rather than a time series.
why_useful: Global Peace Index is a country-level annual safety/instability score that could serve as a coarse macro control for destination-country risk in the same demand-shock family as travel advisories, though it is annual and static rather than point-in-time dated, and is a weaker signal than the State Dept advisory feed above.
themes: Insurance, safety and travel advisories datasets (State Dept advisories history, travel insurance claims, crime by city) as demand shocks
why_all: Global Peace Index is a country-level annual safety/instability score that could serve as a coarse macro control for destination-country risk in the same demand-shock family as travel advisories, though it is annual and static rather than point-in-time dated, and is a weaker signal than the State Dept advisory feed above.

A slower-moving, annual country-level safety/risk index that could serve as a control variable or cross-check against the higher-frequency advisory-level series above when assessing regional demand risk (e.g., LatAm/APAC safety perception shifts).
